STEP 1 - Scene: A top-down photo of a single whole green pear on a white square plate. There are a few small carrot shreds and crumbs on the plate.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The plate is square-ish, about 25 cm across at its widest, so its area is about 25 × 25 × 0.85 ≈ 530 cm² (rounded corners). The pear is about 130 px wide against a plate about 345 px wide, which gives roughly 9 cm wide and 9–10 cm tall.

STEP 3 - Items: One whole green pear. A few carrot shreds, which are very small.

STEP 4 - Area: The pear covers about π × 4.5² ≈ 64 cm², or about 12% of the plate. The carrot shreds cover about 0.2%. Together, food covers about 12% of the plate.

STEP 5 - Volume: The pear is roughly an ellipsoid, 9 cm wide by 9.5 cm tall. Volume ≈ 0.52 × 9 × 9 × 9.5 ≈ 400 ml. The carrot is about 1 ml in total.

STEP 6 - Grams: A whole pear has a density of about 0.95 g/ml, which gives about 380 g. That is heavy for a pear this size, and the pear looks a little tapered, so I reduce the estimate to about 300 g. The carrot comes to about 2 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Pear is about 57 kcal/100 g, so 300 g gives about 171 kcal. Carrot is about 41 kcal/100 g, so 2 g gives about 1 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A medium pear weighs about 180–250 g, and this one looks a bit larger. 300 g is acceptable, though perhaps slightly high, so I settle on about 270 g.

Total: about 272 g and about 155 kcal.
